title: LLM literacy bridges — personal reading & quick experiments
content:
Context / intent:
Quick-running personal notebook for synthesizing papers, blogs, and conference talks into tangible small experiments I can run in afternoons. The goal: translate academic & product writing into concrete checks we can run against hosted + dedicated deployments so PMs / SEs can reason about tradeoffs.

Structure of this note:
- Short summary bullets for each item I read/viewed
- Two-line takeaways (what surprised me, what could be shipped)
- Small experiment ideas (5–60m) and acceptance checks
- Open questions I’ll ask on weekly sync or Slack

1) "Disentangling Retrieval Contexts" — workshop paper + talk (NeurIPS workshop, 2026)
- Summary: authors instrumented retrieval augmentation for multi-hop QA and found that retrieval order + contrastive reranking changes the model's reliance on retrieval versus parametric memory. They measured hallucination spikes when irrelevant but high-similarity passages were present.
- Two-line takeaway: retrieval quality gating is as important as retriever recall; low-precision retrieval can actively degrade answers.
- Quick experiment: take a small RAG pipeline on hosted (gpt-3.5-like) and dedicated (vicuna-13b-quant) with 50 test prompts. For each prompt, inject 0, 1, or 3 high-similarity but irrelevant passages and measure F1 + hallucination count.
- Acceptance: delta(F1) < 8% with injected noise for our baseline retriever; hallucination events logged in eval dashboard with examples.

2) Blog: "Why function calling helps reduce drift" (engineering blog, July 2026)
- Summary: structured function calls reduce token-level ambiguity and let downstream systems validate before side effects. Example: date normalization and billing queries.
- Surprising bit: even small schema mismatches (field order, optional vs required) triggered more fallbacks than I expected.
- Small ship: add a shim that converts common legacy field names -> canonical names before sending to model. Add a canary route for 10% of traffic.

3) ICLR talk: "KV cache sharding heuristics for heterogeneous GPUs"
- Summary: framing: shard by key frequency distribution rather than model-layer. Heuristics reduce cross-GPU sync by 25% on long contexts.
- Takeaway for us: Dedicated pools with heterogeneous GPUs might benefit from frequency-based placement. Could be a knob in autoscaler.
- 30m check: run a microbench in private cluster using small LLaMA derivative, emulate skewed key-frequency and measure wall-clock latency and GPU-to-GPU bandwidth.

4) Short survey: "Human-in-the-loop safety checks for LLMs" (meta-synthesis doc)
- Summary: mix of gating strategies: pre-output filters, token-level monitors, and post-output human review flows. Cost/latency tradeoffs are key.
- Ship idea: add a "review-required" flag to Redwood Console rollout rules that routes low-confidence outputs to human queue (simulate with dataset and a cheap classifier).

Notes to self / heuristics I want to remember:
- When reading a systems paper, always extract the workload distribution assumptions (seq len, tokens/sec, cache hit rates). Those assumptions determine whether a trick generalizes to our hosted workloads.
- For product-facing writeups, include an explicit cost delta line: CPU/GPU + tokens. PMs care about $/1M tokens.
- Small, observable experiments beat conceptual arguments in product reviews.

Mini reading list (links to read next week):
- "Contrastive retriever failure modes" — arXiv (2026).
- "Operationalizing function schemas: lessons learned" — engineering notes (internal).
- "Adaptive batching for tail latency" — systems workshop (2025).
- A short Ops checklist: "What to measure for a new model rollout" — I want to formalize this into a 1-page checklist for SEs.

Open questions / things to ask the team:
- To SRE: what telemetry do we already have for "low-confidence outputs" by model? Can we get per-route confidence histograms?
- To Retrieval people: can we do on-the-fly retriever precision diagnostics in production (sampled)?
- To Product: how much latency increase is acceptable for human-review flows in enterprise vs PLG tiers?

Actionable micro-tasks (ranked):
- [ ] Prototype noisy-retrieval injection experiment on hosted sandbox (2–3h). (Priority: high)
- [ ] Add small field-name shim for function-calling schema (1h) + canary route (1h). (Priority: medium)
- [ ] Write 1-page checklist for model rollout metrics (30–60m). (Priority: high)
- [ ] Schedule 15m sync with Rina to align on retrieval diagnostics (Priority: high)

Quick sketches / TODO notes (stream-of-consciousness):
- Could we expose a "retrieval-precision" slider in the Console that trades recall->precision by adjusting re-ranker threshold? UX: two knobs, recommended presets: conservative / balanced / exploratory.
- If adding human-review routing, cost center tagging is critical so enterprises can track review cost.
- If implementing KV frequency sharding, need a metric: per-step cross-device sync bytes. Instrumentation path: runtime -> telemetry -> Console per-model chart.

Random scribbles and questions to resolve:
- How noisy is our production retriever (hosted API)? ask QA for 100 sample sessions.
- Do we have an internal dataset of hallucination-labeled cases? (I think CS has some).

End notes: keep this file intentionally informal. When something stabilizes, extract into a proper Confluence summary and link back.

Markers: alexis/2026-10-04 initial; updates 2026-10-10 added experiment checklist + linked artifacts.
